nodes.name: PACP hollow nanosphere synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.38 mL aniline, 0.29 mL pyrrole and 0.06 g Triton X-100 was dissolved in 60 mL of distilled water. Then the solution was placed in ice-bath and mixed thoroughly under magnetic stirring and ultrasonicated for 30 min, leading to formation of a homogeneous solution. In the next step, for performing the polymerization process, the precooled aqueous solution of APS (0.2 mmol) was added to the above precooled mixture in one portion and solution mixed thoroughly with magnetic stirring for 5 min until a homogeneous solution is obtained. Afterward, the resultant solution was transferred into a capped bottle and keep in 0°C for 12 h without agitation. Finally, the product was washed several times with DI water until the filtrate aqueous became colorless. After that, the solid product was collected from filtration paper and dried at 60°C for 24 h.

nodes.name: N-HCNSs carbonization
nodes.procedure: Dried PACP was transferred to a ceramic boat. The boat was placed in a quartz tube, which was fixed in a tube furnace. Before starting the heating process, air was evacuated by continuous flow of argon for 30 min. Then furnace temperature was raised to 900°C with a heating rate of 1°C min⁻¹ for 8 h under the argon atmosphere to obtain a black powder. The carbonized products were collected after cooling down to the room temperature.
nodes.source_text: N-HCNSs were synthesized by direct carbonization of PACP hollow spheres... collected after cooling down to the room temperature.

nodes.name: NiO-NSs@N-HCNSs hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 20 mg of the prepared N-HCNSs was dispersed in 20 mL of DI-water and continuously ultra-sonicated for 30 min. Then, 4.2 g of NiSO4·6H2O and 0.745 g of Na2S2O3 were dissolved in 25 mL of DI-water and the prepared solution slowly added to the N-HCNSs solution and the mixture was ultra-sonicated until obtaining a homogeneous solution. After that, 2 mL of ammonia (25%wt) was added drop wise to the mild stirring mixture. The resultant solution was sealed into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and placed in an oven at 120°C for 24 h. After cooling down in room temperature, Ni(OH)2-NSs@N-HCNSs was filtered and washed several times with DI-water and was dried at 60°C overnight.

nodes.name: NiO-NWs@N-HCNSs hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2.58 g of NiSO4·6H2O was dissolved in 30 mL of DI-water and was gently added to the as-prepared N-HCNSs solution. Then, 10 mL of NaOH aqueous solution was added to this mixture. In the next step, the prepared sample was transferred to the autoclave and kept at 120°C for 24 h. After performing the hydrothermal processes and washing the product with DI-water and placing in an oven at 80°C for 12 h, the Ni(OH)2-NWs@N-HCNSs were obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: PACP shows nanospheres with 90 nm diameter. N-HCNSs retains hollow spherical morphology after carbonization. NiO-NSs@N-HCNSs shows flower-like nanosheets ~10 nm diameter. NiO-NWs@N-HCNSs shows nanowires 60 nm diameter, 100 nm length.
nodes.evidence_snippet: PACP demonstrated a well-defined nanosphere structure with an average diameter of 90 nm ... N-HCNSs with relatively smooth surface and uniform particle size distribution ... NiO-NSs@N-HCNSs ... hierarchical interconnected nanosheets with a diameter around 10 nm ... NiO-NWs@N-HCNSs ... wires have 3D structures with an average diameter of 60 nm and length of 100 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: N-HCNSs shows hollow structure with outer diameter ~50 nm and inner diameter ~30 nm. NiO-NSs@N-HCNSs and NiO-NWs@N-HCNSs confirm hollow spherical cores with nanowire and nanosheet shells.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2A and B ... reveals an empty core and a shell, i.e. hollow structure with the outer and inner diameter of about 50 and 30 nm, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: N-HCNSs shows peaks at 23.35° and 46.3° (002, 101 planes). NiO nanostructures show peaks at 37°, 43.1°, 62.7° corresponding to (111), (200), (220) planes of NiO (JCPDS 78-0423). NiO-NWs@N-HCNSs shows higher crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: N-HCNs shows two characteristic peaks placed at 23.35° and 46.3°, which can be attributed to its 002 and 101 planes ... NiO nanostructures ... three major diffraction peaks at 2θ values about 37°, 43.1°, and 62.7° that are indexed to (111), (200), and (220) plans of NiO.

nodes.characterization_summary: N-HCNSs shows OH at ~3230 cm⁻¹, CO at 1234 cm⁻¹, CN at 1183 and 1398 cm⁻¹. NiO composites show Ni-O stretching at 446-596 cm⁻¹ confirming NiO formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: N-HCNs show two absorption bands at ~3230 cm⁻¹ and 1234 cm⁻¹ ... absorption bands around 1183 cm⁻¹ and 1398 cm⁻¹, which are related to the characteristic absorbance of single CN bonds ... NiO-NSs@N-HCNSs and NiO-NWs@N-HCNSs, absorption bands observed ... 446 cm⁻¹ to 596 cm⁻¹ are attributed to the stretching vibrations of NiO.

nodes.characterization_summary: N-HCNSs/GCE shows low Rct. NiO nanocomposites show slightly increased Rct due to semiconductor properties of NiO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: N-HCNSs/GCE shows smaller semicircle diameter and consequently low Rct. After the surface modification of N-HCNSs with NiO nanostructure, a little increase was observed in the semicircle diameter.
